San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey’s newborn son, Roman, is attending his first NFL game on Sunday, when the 49ers face the Las Vegas Raiders at home.

This means McCaffrey’s wife, Olivia Culpo, has to navigate handling their two children during the game, which can create some unique challenges.

Culpo is taking a relatively carefree attitude towards breastfeeding, as shown through several comments she made in an Instagram post on Saturday.

When explaining what was in the bag she brings when taking her son places, Culpo said, “This is a muslin swaddle, but I leave this one loose, as more of like a, keep it over you while you’re breastfeeding, so nobody sees your boobs. Although, who really cares anyway?”

She later added, “I actually love breastfeeding, to be honest.”

On Sunday, Culpo posted a TikTok video where she detailed the outfit she was wearing to San Francisco’s game and spoke more about breastfeeding.

“This is legitimately my postpartum uniform. [Starting] out with a bodysuit, [with a] scoop-neck so I can breastfeed easily,” Culpo said.

“I used to think I was high-maintenance until I started breastfeeding, then I realized how high-maintenance my boobs are,” she later added while showing off the 49ers jacket she “stole” from 49ers tight end George Kittle’s wife, Claire.

Culpo and McCaffrey had a daughter named Colette in the summer of 2025, so none of these challenges are new for Culpo.

But that doesn’t mean they’re easy to deal with in public.

news.originalContent:

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said the GOP only has itself to blame for the youth’s turn toward socialism after voters 30 and under swung left during last week’s midterm elections.

The term-limited governor blamed “corporatist Republicans” who bend government toward favored industries and companies for young Americans’ negativity toward capitalism and increasingly positive outlook on socialism during an appearance on “The Sage Steele Show.”

“Young people have a very positive view of socialism compared to capitalism. The question is, why is that?” DeSantis said Wednesday — just a day after Democrats seized both chambers of Congress by overwhelming margins.

“Some of it is the education in our universities. But I think a big part of that is, what they’re comparing is not free enterprise versus socialism. What they’re comparing is how government gets involved in business, and you have crony capitalism.”

“The best kind of indirect supporters of socialism are some of these corporatist Republicans who propagate these crony policies,” he went on, arguing such individuals turn off young people.

For a Republican like himself, DeSantis said, a socialist on the ballot is an easy no. Less certain, he said, is whether the label still scandalizes “the broader electorate who aren’t as partisan.”

“If it’s cronyism versus socialism, there’s going to be enough people who are going to choose socialism,” he warned.

Tuesday’s results suggest the “socialist” label frightened few.

Republicans spent much of the cycle tying vulnerable lefty Democrats to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist.

“House Republicans will make Zohran Mamdani famous in battleground races next November,” the National Republican Congressional Committee promised in an October 2025 memo, according to Axios.

By Wednesday, DeSantis had already called the elections “close to an extinction-level event for Republicans in many parts of the country.”

On X, he predicted the Senate may stay out of GOP hands until 2032.

The results bore out his gloom. Democrats took Republican-held Senate seats in Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina.

In Florida, Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.) won the governor’s mansion by just over a point, edging Democrat David Jolly to succeed the term-limited DeSantis.

His case against cronyism predates the drubbing. In September, he told the Heartland Institute that crony capitalism has “warmed over socialism.”

Nowhere was the rout steeper than among the voters he was describing. Those under 30 went for Democratic House candidates 66% to 31%, according to a preliminary estimate from Tufts University’s CIRCLE — up from a 14-point Democratic margin in the 2024 House exit poll.

The final result didn’t go in Sadiku Ibine Ayo’s favor, but it was a memorable return to the Garden nonetheless for the former St. John’s co-captain and Rick Pitino favorite.

Prior to tipoff, St. John’s honored Ibine Ayo with a tribute video, and the Johnnies fans gave him a loud ovation.

St John’s welcomes back Sadiku Ibine Ayo #sjubb pic.twitter.com/ZzpG5dnNJB

“It was nice, seeing what I did here is being appreciated,” Ibine Ayo said after the Red Storm’s 104-65 rout of his Gaels on Sunday in front of 13,753 at the Garden. “The fans applauding was nice and I appreciate them for that.

“It was amazing. I’m always the one telling my teammates after every game to clap to the fans. Whenever I see a St. John’s fan out, I tell them I appreciate what they’re doing.”

Ibine Ayo started his college career with Pitino at Iona, came with him to Queens and spent the past three years at St. John’s. He returned to Iona for his final season to play major minutes. He plans to play professionally overseas.

Ibine Ayo and Pitino remain very close. Pitino considers him another son, and his grandchildren refer to him as “Uncle Diku.”

There was another reason Sunday was special for Ibine Ayo, who grew up in Ghana and attended high school in The Bronx at Our Saviour Lutheran. His father, Ibine Ayo, was in the crowd.

“It’s amazing, man. This is the first time he’s seen me play basketball,” Sadiku Ibine Ayo, who scored 11 points in defeat, said. “It’s something, coming from where I came from, I’ll always cherish.”

Forward Babacar Sane (ankle) didn’t play. The injury doesn’t appear serious. … Godson Okokoh, a four-star forward recruit from Bella Vista College Prep (Ariz.), was in attendance for the game.

Philadelphia’s branch of the Democratic Socialists of America is claiming that its anti-Israel movement is being repressed because of the backlash against its Sunday boycott of Jewish-owned businesses in the City of Brotherly Love.

The DSA group doubled-down on its poorly planned boycott, which was held on the eve of the Kristallnacht Nazi night of terror, claiming the outrage against Sunday’s effort was unwarranted and belittled the boycotters’ message.

“From the Senator Fetterman and Congressman Boyle to Governor Shapiro, Mayor Parker, and Council President Johnson, politicians have joined a chorus of bad-faith and dangerous conflation of antisemitism with anti-Zionism and invoking comparisons of the Kristallnacht that trivialize trauma and suppress political speech,” the group said in a statement.

“These condemnations were not good-faith conversations about tactics.”

The Philly DSA also appeared to be surprised by the backlash, given last week’s blue wave at the midterms, which the group claimed was evidence of “growing opposition to Israel’s genocide in Palestine.

“What we’ve seen instead is an unacceptable use of political power, designed to delegitimize and chill acts of solidarity in the fight for Palestinian liberation, weaponized against the very people who helped put these politicians in office,” the Philly DSA fumed.

Sunday’s boycott, organized by Philly Bike On Your Left,  targeted several Jewish-owned businesses in the city’s Rittenhouse Square.

But the demonstration was called off early when the boycotters were met with hundreds of counter-protesters who came out in support of the restaurants.

The organizers said the boycott was shut down over safety concerns and claimed the event has been “grossly misrepresented.”

One masked man admitted to The Post that he didn’t know why Mac Mart, one of the targeted businesses, was chosen despite not having any connections to Israel.

“I don’t know. I’m not a spokesperson for the movement,” he said after calling on people to do their research when it comes to organizing boycotts.

Marti Lieberman, 37, co-owner of Mac Mart, suggested that her business was targeted simply because she was Jewish and wore a Star of David necklace while working behind the counter.

LANDOVER, Md. — Just when the Los Angeles Rams thought their injury nightmare was finally behind them, another dark cloud appeared over their locker room Sunday afternoon.

All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua reportedly suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap of their 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of the damage.

According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Rams do not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but Monday’s imaging will provide a clearer picture.

All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A

The news comes as a potentially devastating blow for a Rams team that has finally found its footing, winning three consecutive games to climb above .500 for the first time this season.

Interestingly, there were no obvious signs of trouble when the California Post spoke with Nacua following the game.

The Rams’ star receiver was standing, smiling and displaying his usual jovial personality, hardly resembling a player who had just suffered a potentially significant knee injury.

Puka Nacua after the Rams victory. He talked about going into the medical tent after being flagged for concussion protocol, but mentioned nothing about the knee injury and seemed okay to me. pic.twitter.com/jdxNjr0cyD

Earlier in the game, Nacua had another injury scare after running a deep route on an incomplete third-down pass. He immediately entered the blue medical tent, raising concerns about his health.

When asked about that sequence afterward, Nacua explained that he had been flagged for a potential concussion. He subsequently returned to action.

“I called in for concussion protocol,” said Nacua. “It was a deep ball and I fell down, but nothing to do with a head injury.”

Apparently, his injury troubles weren’t finished.

Nacua’s latest setback comes amid a season in which injuries have ravaged the Rams’ roster, making his availability even more critical as Los Angeles attempts to salvage its Super Bowl aspirations.

Head coach Sean McVay is expected to address the injury when he speaks with reporters Monday.

news.originalTitle: Lopez double fires Barcelona to win at Atletico Madrid
news.title: Lopez double fires Barcelona to win at Atletico Madrid
news.originalSummary:
Fermin Lopez brace has Barcelona come from behind to win 2-1 at Atletico Madrid to go three points clear in La Liga.

Fermin Lopez scored twice as Barcelona overcame an early deficit at Atletico Madrid to win 2-1 and go three points clear at the top of La Liga.

Barca’s win takes them three points clear of second-placed Real Madrid and five ahead of Atletico, in third, after 12 games.

news.originalContent:
Fermin Lopez brace has Barcelona come from behind to win 2-1 at Atletico Madrid to go three points clear in La Liga.

Fermin Lopez scored twice as Barcelona overcame an early deficit at Atletico Madrid to win 2-1 and go three points clear at the top of La Liga.

Barca’s win takes them three points clear of second-placed Real Madrid and five ahead of Atletico, in third, after 12 games.

Giuliano Simeone opened the scoring in the 10th minute for the home side, turning home a close range volley from Julian Alvarez’s cross from the left.

The home side had a series of early chances as they sought to register an eighth straight win, but Fermin swept in an equaliser on the cusp of halftime after a ball broke to him in the box.

Lamine Yamal set up Fermin’s second goal in the 66th minute with an incisive pass, and Lopez fired past Jan Oblak with a first-time finish to silence the Metropolitano and secure a fifth straight away league win over Atleti for the first time.

“It was a very difficult match. The first half was tough, but we managed to come from behind and secure the win,” Barcelona midfielder Lopez told La Liga TV after the match.

“I think we were not being clinical enough. After the goal, we gained more confidence.

“Lamine [Yamal] has been very good. His pass for the second goal was half the goal itself. I’m very happy,” Lopez said.

“We wanted to go into the break as league leaders and get three points. The equaliser lifted a weight off our shoulders, and we had more control.

“We knew at halftime that we had to continue playing the way we finished the first half. I think the team produced an incredible second half, both defensively and offensively. We’re very happy.”

“It was a very difficult match. The first half was tough, but we managed to come from behind and secure the win,” Barcelona midfielder Lopez told La Liga TV after the match.

“I think we were not being clinical enough. After the goal, we gained more confidence.

“Lamine [Yamal] has been very good. His pass for the second goal was half the goal itself. I’m very happy,” Lopez said.

“We wanted to go into the break as league leaders and get three points. The equaliser lifted a weight off our shoulders, and we had more control.

“We knew at halftime that we had to continue playing the way we finished the first half. I think the team produced an incredible second half, both defensively and offensively. We’re very happy.”

A hot air balloon made an emergency landing in the backyard of a California home on Saturday.

Menifee resident Maryam Dandan captured the bright blue balloon, decorated with gold stars and a crescent moon, as it drifted toward the ground.

She said it was her husband who first noticed the giant blue balloon.

“I was in this room, and my husband came in, and he looked out this window, and he said, ‘Oh, my gosh. Look at the hot air balloon,'” Dandan told ABC 7.

She said that it appeared as if the balloon was making an emergency landing because of a tear.

“It looked like it was an emergency landing. And when we got closer, the hot air balloon looked like it might have had some kind of tear,” she added.

The details of the balloon’s operator are unknown at the moment. It is also not clear how many people were in its basket when it made the emergency landing.

This isn’t the first such landing in California. In April this year, a similar-looking balloon had landed in a backyard in Temecula.

A total of 13 people were on board, including a couple, Brianna Avalos and her husband, who were celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary.

Avalos had said at the time that the pilot informed passengers that he needed to make an emergency landing because of low fuel and a shift in winds.

After disembarking the passengers in the backyard of the Temecula home, the pilot took off again with the balloon and brought it down nearby on a public street, where it was officially dismantled, PBS reported.

Lamine Yamal never seems to be cold or sore on the soccer field.

The 19-year-old is a few months removed from winning the 2026 World Cup with Spain and is currently tearing up La Liga with FC Barcelona, tallying 10 goals and 7 assists in 11 league games.

Off the field, Yamal is still in a high-profile relationship with his model girlfriend, Spanish model Ines Garcia.

Garcia posted to her Instagram story on Saturday that provided an unfortunate health update.

The post showed Garcia wearing some sort of cream on her nose, around her nostrils, and was captioned (in translated Spanish), “It had been a long time since I’d had a herpes outbreak… Do you remember about a year ago??

“I was getting at least one a month… 😢 / Yesterday I woke up with one on my nose, and I’ve been looking like this 24 hours a day.”

Garcia received praise for her openness about her herpes diagnosis, as it can be a difficult and stigmatized subject to speak about, especially for someone with a huge following like Garcia.

Yamal helped FC Barcelona defeat Atlético Madrid in La Liga today, 2-1.

news.originalContent:
Pope Leo XIV’s visit marks the first papal trip to Argentina in nearly four decades, amid tensions with the Milei government.

Argentinian President Javier Milei has welcomed the head of the Catholic Church, Pope Leo XIV, upon his arrival at Jorge Newbery airport near Buenos Aires.

Milei and his sister, presidential secretary Karina Milei, greeted the pope on Sunday amid tensions between the government and Argentina’s Catholic Church over austerity measures.

Prior to his arrival, the pope spent three days in Uruguay, the first stop on his tour of Latin America.

He is the first pontiff to visit Argentina in nearly four decades, since John Paul II’s trip in 1987.

“Without a doubt, it gives us great joy that this pope is visiting us,” said Jorge Silanes, religious director at the Pequeno Cottolengo Don Orione, a home for people with disabilities in the Buenos Aires province.

In Argentina, Pope Leo’s schedule includes attending a welcome ceremony at Plaza San Martin and a meeting with Milei at the Casa Rosada, the official presidential palace.

But the pontiff’s visit comes amid shrinking membership in the Catholic Church in Latin America, as well as a sometimes fractious relationship with politicians like Milei.

Catholics comprise the largest religious group in Latin America, with as many as 425 million people identifying with the church.

But their numbers have shrunk over the last decade. A Pew Research Center survey found that, in Argentina, the percentage of self-identifying Catholics slipped from 71 percent in the 2013-2014 year to 58 percent a decade later.

Milei himself has suggested he considered converting to Judaism, though he was raised in the Catholic faith.

The Catholic Church has also criticised Milei’s austerity measures, which included slashing social spending and safety-net programmes for the poor.

Milei has defended the budget cuts as necessary to bring inflation under control.

Some members of the Catholic clergy, however, have taken a visible role in the protests against Milei’s measures.

Leo, 71, the first US-born pope, will remain in Argentina until Wednesday and meet with officials, diplomats and civil society representatives.

He will also visit a prison and celebrate mass in Buenos Aires, Lujan, and the province of Cordoba, before travelling to Peru, where he spent years serving as a bishop.

The previous pope, Francis, was born in Buenos Aires in 1936 and was the first pope from the Americas, but he never visited his home country as head of the Catholic Church. Francis died in 2025.

He and Milei had a notably contentious relationship, with the Argentinian president calling the late pontiff a “communist” and an “imbecile who defends social justice”.

“Leo is going to make the visit that Francis never did,” said Reverend Lorenzo “Toto” de Vedia, who works with poor communities in a neighbourhood of Buenos Aires.

news.originalContent:
Huang has confirmed he had been having an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.

United States-based chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its chief executive officer, billionaire Jensen Huang, after he confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence.

In an announcement on Sunday, Nvidia said the probe would be conducted by a “committee of independent directors” with outside counsel.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board of directors said.

It said the board continued to have “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team”. Huang will continue to lead Nvidia during the probe.

The investigation follows a report in The New York Times last month that Jensen may have been the target of a Chinese espionage plot.

China and the US have been in competition to dominate key tech sectors like artificial intelligence (AI).

Amid the AI boom, Nvidia has seen demand for its chips and programming interfaces explode, resulting in the company being valued in the trillions of dollars.

For years, the US has sought to restrict the export of advanced chips to China, fearing the Asian superpower could gain an edge over its technology and military sectors.

But on October 29, The New York Times said it had obtained exclusive information that a Chinese woman named Alice Huang, or Huang Le, sought to cultivate close ties with Jensen Huang in an effort to glean information about Nvidia’s technology.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, has denied any allegations of spying in the case.

The New York Times also reported that Alice Huang’s employer, Megaspeed, had become one of Nvidia’s largest buyers, purchasing some $4.8bn in equipment from the US firm.

Jensen Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, who is of no relation, spurred fierce bipartisan backlash in the US Congress in the aftermath of the report.

“For months, bipartisan members of Congress have raised concerns about NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips going to China,” Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote in a statement.

“NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers. And we need to pass bipartisan legislation we have ready to stop advanced American technology from going to China.”

Republican lawmakers in the House of Representatives also called on Huang to appear and testify before Congress about the affair on November 18.

“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” Republicans John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford said in a statement.

In an email to Nvidia staff on Sunday, Huang had admitted to having an extramarital relationship.

“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse ‌for what I did,” Huang said.

Nvidia has grown rapidly in recent years with the rise of AI, producing chips for large language models developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google.

Huang has also been closely working with US President Donald Trump since the Republican leader returned to office in 2025.

In August of that year, the Trump administration announced it would take a 15 percent cut of certain Nvidia chip sales to China.

Trump reportedly bought as much as $1.6m in Nvidia stock and sold about $1m in August, ahead of November’s midterm elections.

After the midterm races last Tuesday, stocks for AI-related companies, including Nvidia, tumbled in reaction to widespread Republican losses.

Trump has pushed back against calls to regulate AI companies, but many Democrats during the midterms campaigned on placing restrictions on the companies, including on the construction of data centres.

Nvidia lost $450bn in market value in a single trading day last week, but it rebounded on Friday, regaining 4 percent of its losses.

news.originalContent:
The two have business ties going back decades, and White has helped Trump reach out to younger voters.

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White is set to meet United States President Donald Trump on Monday to discuss taking the job of White House press secretary.

Trump announced the offer on Saturday, days after his Republican Party suffered record losses in midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, the president praised White as “a violent Fighter and Warrior” who would bring along leading UFC fighters as “assistants” to “defend us against the Lunatic Left”.

But it remains unclear how serious the offer is. In a news conference on Saturday, White confirmed he would travel to Washington, DC, to meet with Trump. But he also signalled concerns about his existing workload.

“I got a lot of jobs already,” White, a Trump ally and donor, said. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that.”

White also posted a photo to Instagram Stories of himself standing behind the White House podium. Its caption read, “On to the next chapter.”

Trump, too, posted his own AI-generated memes about the potential hire.

On Sunday, he shared an animated cartoon of White in the White House briefing room, flanked by a row of fighters. One of them body-slams a reporter who asks, “Is Trump a threat to democracy?”

The press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s brief tenure ended ‌last ⁠month. She left the post within five days of being hired after facing criticism that she presented herself as a lawyer without being licensed in the US.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August, citing the needs of her growing family.

But why is the head of a mixed martial arts franchise being considered for the new public face of the Trump administration? Al Jazeera explains that and more in this brief explainer.

A former bouncer and small-time boxer, White began his career as a businessman by opening a boxing gym in Boston where he trained other fighters.

He later moved to Las Vegas, where he continued to run gyms and manage emerging fighters.

The UFC was founded in 1993, at about the time White resettled in Las Vegas. The organisation sought to offer an arena for fighters from different disciplines – from boxing to wrestling to jujitsu – to face each other in “no-holds-barred” competition.

In 2001, White convinced two casino magnate friends to buy the UFC for $2m and name him president. Since then, he has built the company up through big fights and lucrative pay-per-view television deals.

He has been a fixture in the UFC in the more than two decades since. White has been credited with turning the fledgling franchise into a global business that brought mixed martial arts into the mainstream.

In 2016, the UFC was sold for $4bn, and in 2023, White became its CEO after a merger with World Wrestling Entertainment valued at some $21bn.

White has been a longtime supporter of Trump, appearing by his side at campaign events for nearly a decade.

Trump, in turn, has a history of hosting UFC fights as far back as 2001. At the time, UFC was struggling against criticism that the sport was too violent.

White had just taken up his position as UFC president, and he and Trump came to an agreement to host that year’s UFC championship at Trump’s Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

The next year, the UFC returned to the Taj Mahal.

Speaking in support of Trump at the 2016 Republican National Convention, White recalled how the early collaboration helped open doors for the UFC, making other venues more accessible.

“No arenas wanted us,” White said at the time. “This guy reached out, and he’s always been a friend to me.”

The 2016 election cycle would mark Trump’s first successful bid for public office. In 2018, White was invited to visit the White House during Trump’s inaugural term as president.

During the 2020 elections, White again endorsed Trump as he sought a second term as president. White also donated $1m to Trump’s campaign and was a key speaker at the Republican Party’s national convention that year.

“I’ve known this man for 20 years. We’ve actually become even closer since he’s become the president of the United States,” White told supporters at a rally in Colorado. “He’s a fighter. He loves this country. He’s doing great things for this country, and we’ve got to win this election again.”

Trump lost the 2020 race to Democrat Joe Biden. But four years later, in 2024, he launched another re-election bid, and successfully won a second term.

During that campaign, Trump credited White with helping him connect with younger voters.

“He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids,” Trump told Time Magazine in May. “I was being interviewed by 20-year-old kids. I’m saying, ‘Where the hell did you meet these people?’ They’re called influencers.”

Experts say Trump’s 2024 campaign benefitted significantly from his UFC connections.

Ahead of his victory, Trump courted influencers like UFC fan Theo Von and UFC host Joe Rogan, whose podcast boasts about 11 million listeners per episode.

Trump has also used his second term as president to elevate the UFC’s profile, weaving one of its events into plans to celebrate the 250th US Independence Day.

Dubbed “UFC Freedom 250”, the tournament was given unusual access to national monuments for a commercial event.

White, for instance, hosted a weigh-in for fighters on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, with uniformed military personnel standing as an honour guard. The fights themselves were held on the lawn of the White House.

Trump called the event “one of the most exciting days in the history of our fabled White House”.

But critics warned the event could constitute a conflict of interest: In the months before the fight, Trump reportedly bought up to $50,000 of stock in TKO Holding, the UFC’s parent company.

A lawsuit also challenged the UFC’s use of public facilities, calling the event “deeply corrupt”.

Some opposition figures have dismissed Trump’s idea of appointing White as press secretary as a way to distract attention from the midterm elections.

During the November 3 elections, Trump’s Republican Party suffered record losses, losing majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Melat Kiros, a Democrat elected to represent Colorado in the House, said on Saturday that Trump’s offer to White “demonstrates how deeply unserious this man is, how ridiculous this administration is”.

Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, meanwhile, said Trump’s choice raised questions about the president’s wellbeing.

“It would be really funny if it wasn’t dangerous, if he wasn’t the president,” Kelly said. “Countries around the world are continuing to laugh at us because of what he’s doing.”

There has also been some speculation that Trump may have tapped the wrong Dana White.

A woman by the same name formerly worked as a Pentagon spokesperson during Trump’s first term. She has denied being approached for the press secretary role.

“To everyone texting me congratulations: thank you, but you have the wrong Dana White,” she wrote on LinkedIn.
news.content:
The two have business ties going back decades, and White has helped Trump reach out to younger voters.

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White is set to meet United States President Donald Trump on Monday to discuss taking the job of White House press secretary.

Trump announced the offer on Saturday, days after his Republican Party suffered record losses in midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, the president praised White as “a violent Fighter and Warrior” who would bring along leading UFC fighters as “assistants” to “defend us against the Lunatic Left”.

But it remains unclear how serious the offer is. In a news conference on Saturday, White confirmed he would travel to Washington, DC, to meet with Trump. But he also signalled concerns about his existing workload.

“I got a lot of jobs already,” White, a Trump ally and donor, said. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that.”

White also posted a photo to Instagram Stories of himself standing behind the White House podium. Its caption read, “On to the next chapter.”

Trump, too, posted his own AI-generated memes about the potential hire.

On Sunday, he shared an animated cartoon of White in the White House briefing room, flanked by a row of fighters. One of them body-slams a reporter who asks, “Is Trump a threat to democracy?”

The press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s brief tenure ended ‌last ⁠month. She left the post within five days of being hired after facing criticism that she presented herself as a lawyer without being licensed in the US.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August, citing the needs of her growing family.

But why is the head of a mixed martial arts franchise being considered for the new public face of the Trump administration? Al Jazeera explains that and more in this brief explainer.

A former bouncer and small-time boxer, White began his career as a businessman by opening a boxing gym in Boston where he trained other fighters.

He later moved to Las Vegas, where he continued to run gyms and manage emerging fighters.

The UFC was founded in 1993, at about the time White resettled in Las Vegas. The organisation sought to offer an arena for fighters from different disciplines – from boxing to wrestling to jujitsu – to face each other in “no-holds-barred” competition.

In 2001, White convinced two casino magnate friends to buy the UFC for $2m and name him president. Since then, he has built the company up through big fights and lucrative pay-per-view television deals.

He has been a fixture in the UFC in the more than two decades since. White has been credited with turning the fledgling franchise into a global business that brought mixed martial arts into the mainstream.

In 2016, the UFC was sold for $4bn, and in 2023, White became its CEO after a merger with World Wrestling Entertainment valued at some $21bn.

White has been a longtime supporter of Trump, appearing by his side at campaign events for nearly a decade.

Trump, in turn, has a history of hosting UFC fights as far back as 2001. At the time, UFC was struggling against criticism that the sport was too violent.

White had just taken up his position as UFC president, and he and Trump came to an agreement to host that year’s UFC championship at Trump’s Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

The next year, the UFC returned to the Taj Mahal.

Speaking in support of Trump at the 2016 Republican National Convention, White recalled how the early collaboration helped open doors for the UFC, making other venues more accessible.

“No arenas wanted us,” White said at the time. “This guy reached out, and he’s always been a friend to me.”

The 2016 election cycle would mark Trump’s first successful bid for public office. In 2018, White was invited to visit the White House during Trump’s inaugural term as president.

During the 2020 elections, White again endorsed Trump as he sought a second term as president. White also donated $1m to Trump’s campaign and was a key speaker at the Republican Party’s national convention that year.

“I’ve known this man for 20 years. We’ve actually become even closer since he’s become the president of the United States,” White told supporters at a rally in Colorado. “He’s a fighter. He loves this country. He’s doing great things for this country, and we’ve got to win this election again.”

Trump lost the 2020 race to Democrat Joe Biden. But four years later, in 2024, he launched another re-election bid, and successfully won a second term.

During that campaign, Trump credited White with helping him connect with younger voters.

“He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids,” Trump told Time Magazine in May. “I was being interviewed by 20-year-old kids. I’m saying, ‘Where the hell did you meet these people?’ They’re called influencers.”

Experts say Trump’s 2024 campaign benefitted significantly from his UFC connections.

Ahead of his victory, Trump courted influencers like UFC fan Theo Von and UFC host Joe Rogan, whose podcast boasts about 11 million listeners per episode.

Trump has also used his second term as president to elevate the UFC’s profile, weaving one of its events into plans to celebrate the 250th US Independence Day.

Dubbed “UFC Freedom 250”, the tournament was given unusual access to national monuments for a commercial event.

White, for instance, hosted a weigh-in for fighters on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, with uniformed military personnel standing as an honour guard. The fights themselves were held on the lawn of the White House.

Trump called the event “one of the most exciting days in the history of our fabled White House”.

But critics warned the event could constitute a conflict of interest: In the months before the fight, Trump reportedly bought up to $50,000 of stock in TKO Holding, the UFC’s parent company.

A lawsuit also challenged the UFC’s use of public facilities, calling the event “deeply corrupt”.

Some opposition figures have dismissed Trump’s idea of appointing White as press secretary as a way to distract attention from the midterm elections.

During the November 3 elections, Trump’s Republican Party suffered record losses, losing majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Melat Kiros, a Democrat elected to represent Colorado in the House, said on Saturday that Trump’s offer to White “demonstrates how deeply unserious this man is, how ridiculous this administration is”.

Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, meanwhile, said Trump’s choice raised questions about the president’s wellbeing.

“It would be really funny if it wasn’t dangerous, if he wasn’t the president,” Kelly said. “Countries around the world are continuing to laugh at us because of what he’s doing.”

There has also been some speculation that Trump may have tapped the wrong Dana White.

A woman by the same name formerly worked as a Pentagon spokesperson during Trump’s first term. She has denied being approached for the press secretary role.

“To everyone texting me congratulations: thank you, but you have the wrong Dana White,” she wrote on LinkedIn.

منبع تصویر، REUTERS/SAUDI MINISTRY OF MEDIA

تشدید تنش‌ها در یمن و حملات حوثی‌ها به زیرساخت‌های حیاتی عربستان سعودی، آزمونی مهم برای رهبری این کشور ایجاد کرده است.

حملات به فرودگاه‌های ریاض و زیرساخت‌های انرژی، چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰ را تهدید می‌کند؛ برنامه شاخص محمد بن سلمان، ولیعهد عربستان، که هدف آن متنوع‌سازی اقتصاد و تبدیل عربستان سعودی به یکی از مراکز جهانی سرمایه‌گذاری، گردشگری و سرگرمی است.

این حملات همچنین می‌توانند به تلاش‌های عربستان برای ارائه تصویری از ثبات و امنیت آسیب بزنند.

در حالی که حملات ادامه دارد، چهره‌های مخالف حکومت عربستان می‌گویند محمد بن سلمان، حاکم عملی کشور، با «یکی از بزرگ‌ترین بحران‌های» دوران خود روبه‌رو شده است؛ آن هم در شرایطی که به گفته آن‌ها حمایت آمریکا کاهش یافته و کمک دیگر متحدان نیز محدود بوده است.

منبع تصویر، YOUTUBE/AL-ISLAH

احزاب سیاسی در عربستان سعودی ممنوع‌اند و حکومت مخالفت سیاسی را تحمل نمی‌کند.

به همین دلیل، اپوزیسیون سعودی از خارج کشور فعالیت می‌کند و شامل مخالفان اسلام‌گرای سنی، اصلاح‌طلبان لیبرال و طرفدار دموکراسی، فعالان حقوق شیعیان و منتقدان مستقل است.

یکی از سازمان‌یافته‌ترین اشکال اپوزیسیون «حزب مجمع ملی» است که کنشگرانی با پیشینه‌های مختلف را گرد هم آورده است.

رسانه‌های مخالف حکومت نیز وجود دارند، از جمله شبکه‌های تلویزیونی «الاصلاح» و «نبا» که ویدیوهایشان در یوتیوب صدها هزار بار دیده می‌شود.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

با شدت گرفتن حملات حوثی‌ها به عربستان در ماه اکتبر، مخالفان سعودی در تبعید، انتقاد از نحوه مدیریت جنگ از سوی حکومت را افزایش دادند و آن را شکستی توصیف کردند که کشور را بیش از پیش آسیب‌پذیر کرده است.

یحیی عسیری، فعال حقوق بشر و طرفدار دموکراسی، مخالفت قاطع خود را با حضور ریاض در جنگ اعلام کرد و در عین حال هرگونه «آسیب» به مردم، منابع یا زیرساخت‌های عربستان را رد کرد.

او در شبکه اجتماعی ایکس نوشت: «[حوثی‌ها] می‌دانند که ما مردمی تحت ستم و شکست‌ خورده‌ایم... کسانی که رنج می‌برند مردم محروم‌اند، در جنگی که خودشان انتخاب نکرده‌اند.»

او همچنین کشتار غیرنظامیان در همه طرف‌ها، از جمله در ریاض، شهر محاصره‌شده تعز در یمن و شهرهای صنعا و الحدیده تحت کنترل حوثی‌ها را محکوم کرد.

حزب او، «حزب مجمع ملی»، خواستار پایان جنگ شد و از رهبری عربستان خواست «از گرفتن تصمیم‌های بی‌پروا که همه ما را در معرض خطر قرار داده، دست بردارد».

علی الاحمد، مخالف شیعه، نیز از محمد بن سلمان خواست «این جنگ را تمام کند، به توافق برسد... و جان انسان‌ها را نجات دهد».

فواد ابراهیم، نویسنده و فعال شیعه، نیز در ایکس نوشت: «این بازی را متوقف کنید... دیگر کافی است... جز ورشکسته‌ها کسی دروغ‌هایتان را باور نمی‌کند.»

منتقدان همچنین به آنچه حمایت ناکافی آمریکا در جنگ می‌دانند و محدودیت‌های پیمان مکه با ترکیه و پاکستان اشاره کرده‌اند.

هرچند این پیمان به‌عنوان یک اتحاد دفاع متقابل مشابه ناتو معرفی شده بود، آنکارا و اسلام‌آباد تاکنون حمایت قابل توجهی از عربستان ارائه نکرده‌اند.

«صوت الناس»وب‌سایت ضد محمد بن سلمان، این پیمان را «نمایشی» توصیف کرده است.

تشدید درگیری همچنین انتقادها از اولویت‌های داخلی محمد بن سلمان را افزایش داده است.

مخالفان می‌گویند هزینه‌های هنگفت برای سرگرمی و پروژه‌های بزرگ توسعه‌ای به بهای تضعیف امنیت ملی تمام شده است.

درخواست‌ها برای پاسخگویی در فضای آنلاین گسترش یافته و برخی منتقدان می‌گویند محمد بن سلمان میلیاردها دلار در «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰» سرمایه‌گذاری کرده، اما نتوانسته امنیت کشور را حفظ کند.

سعید بن ناصر الغامدی، رئیس گروه حقوق بشری «سند» که بنا بر گزارش‌ها در بریتانیا درخواست پناهندگی کرده، در ۱۱ اکتبر در ایکس نوشت: «[محمد بن سلمان] جنگ [یمن] را آغاز کرد و کل کشور را وارد آن کرد... بعد با [حوثی‌ها در سال ۲۰۲۲] آتش‌بس امضا کرد و با آهنگ‌های سرگرمی، مهمانی‌های رقص و پروژه‌های خیالی آسوده نشست، در حالی که حوثی‌ها خود را برای نبردی طولانی آماده می‌کردند.»

منتقدان دیگر نیز به گسترش فعالیت‌های فرهنگی، رویدادهای ورزشی و کنسرت‌ها در عربستان اشاره کرده‌اند که پیش‌تر نیز با انتقاد روبه‌رو شده بودند.

برخی کاربران شبکه‌های اجتماعی در منطقه گفته‌اند این رویدادها با ارزش‌های اسلامی مغایرت دارند و پرسیده‌اند چرا حکومت «رویدادهای فرهنگی» را بر دفاع و امنیت منطقه‌ای مقدم دانسته است.

گروه مخالف «سعودی باس» گفت «شهروندان عربستان «زیر بار ترس زندگی می‌کنند»، در حالی که حکومت «درهای کشور را به روی رقص و آواز گشوده است».

صفحه «به سوی آزادی» در ایکس که ۱/۲ میلیون دنبال‌کننده دارد، ویدیویی از زنانی با پوشش باز در حال رقص در یک کنسرت منتشر کرد و نوشت: «اگر واقعا در مقابله با حوثی‌ها جدی هستید... این مهمانی‌های فاسد باید متوقف شوند.»

ترکی الشلهوب، روزنامه‌نگار مخالف، به ۱/۷ میلیون دنبال‌کننده خود در ایکس گفت «وعده‌های صنایع دفاعی» زمانی که عربستان با یک آزمون واقعی نظامی روبه‌رو شد «ناپدید شدند».

او پرسید: «پس میلیاردهایی که [به این صنعت] اختصاص داده شده بود کجا رفت؟!»

در میان آنچه مخالفان شکست‌های امنیتی می‌دانند، برخی از آن‌ها درخواست برای کنار رفتن حکومت را نیز شدت بخشیده‌اند.

برخی چهره‌های اپوزیسیون سعودی همچنین تاکید کرده‌اند که جنگ عربستان علیه حوثی‌ها به نفع اسرائیل تمام شده است.

دونالد ترامپ در ۱۶ اکتبر گفت ریاض از دریافت حمایت اسرائیل «بسیار خوشحال» است و عادی‌سازی روابط «بیش از هر زمان دیگری» دوباره مطرح شده است.

عبدالله العوده، عضو«حزب مجمع ملی» و پژوهشگر مقیم آمریکا، این کلیپ را در ایکس با هشتگ «عادی‌سازی خیانت است» به اشتراک گذاشت.

او همچنین هرگونه دخالت آمریکا در جنگ را رد کرد و گفت مردم و زیرساخت‌های عربستان «هزینه» این درگیری را می‌پردازند.

الغامدی نیز در ایکس گفت عربستان میلیاردها دلار را صرف رقص و ورزشگاه‌های فوتبال کرده و همین مسئله باعث شده با شروع حملات حوثی‌ها، برای کمک به اسرائیل روی بیاورد.

یحیی عسیری نیز در پستی در ۱۱ اکتبر گفت «کسانی که به جنگ دامن می‌زنند» فقط ثبات منطقه را تضعیف و «صهیونیست‌ها را تقویت» خواهند کرد.

وب‌سایت «سعودی لیکس» نیز از احتمال نزدیکی عربستان و اسرائیل سخن گفته و مدعی شده است اسرائیل در تازه‌ترین عملیات ضد حوثی‌ها در یمن مشارکت داشته است.

با نزدیک شدن به سال ۲۰۳۰، برنامه اقتصادی محمد بن سلمان برای کشور با موانع بزرگی روبه‌رو شده است.

منتقدان تاکید کرده‌اند که «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰»، طرحی بلندپروازانه برای متنوع کردن اقتصاد وابسته به نفت عربستان،  به ثبات و اعتماد سرمایه‌گذاران وابسته است. دو عاملی که جنگ منطقه‌ای آن‌ها را زیر سوال برده است.

مضاوی الرشید، استاد سعودی-بریتانیایی، در ایکس نوشت در حالی که تحلیلگران غربی «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰» را «ستایش» کرده‌اند، چشم‌انداز اقتصادی ریاض عملا به «موضوعی متعلق به گذشته» تبدیل شده است.

او همچنین گفت محمد بن سلمان «توانایی خود برای کنترل روایت موفقیت و رفاه» در رسانه‌های غربی را از دست داده است.

سعد الفقیه، رهبر «جنبش اصلاح اسلامی در عربستان» مستقر در لندن و مجری شبکه «الاصلاح»، گفت رسانه‌های غربی اکنون رهبری عربستان را «به تمسخر» می‌گیرند.

ترکی الشلهوب نیز در ایکس نوشت تمرکز بر «زرق‌وبرق و ظواهر» کار چندانی برای تامین امنیت شهروندان عربستان انجام نخواهد داد.

در جریان تازه‌ترین تشدید تنش‌ها، گزارش شده است که برخی حساب‌های مخالفان در داخل عربستان مسدود شده‌اند.

به گزارش گاردین، بیش از ۶۰ حساب مخالف سعودی در ایکس در ماه اوت مسدود شدند.

پیش‌تر، در ماه مه، کمیته حفاظت از روزنامه‌نگاران، از سرکوب پوشش رسانه‌ای جنگ با ایران در کشورهای خلیج فارس خبر داد و گفت در عربستان «پوشش مسائل سیاسی حساس به‌عنوان جرم علیه امنیت ملی تلقی می‌شود».

همان ماه، گروه حقوق بشری «سند» مستقر در بریتانیا گفت مقام‌های سعودی حساب‌های مخالفان را در تیک‌تاک، اسنپ‌چت و متا مسدود کرده‌اند و در تلاش‌اند این محدودیت‌ها را به ایکس نیز گسترش دهند.

در ماه اکتبر، هم‌زمان با حملات حوثی‌ها به زیرساخت‌های عربستان، غانم الدوسری، مخالف و کمدین مقیم بریتانیا، ریاض را متهم کرد که پس از انتشار مطلبی درباره قربانیان حمله حوثی‌ها به فرودگاه بین‌المللی ملک خالد، حساب او در ایکس را مسدود کرده است.

او با طعنه گفت: «با این حال، [عربستان سعودی] نتوانست موشک‌ها و پهپادهای حوثی‌ها را مسدود کند.»

منبع تصویر، REUTERS/SAUDI MINISTRY OF MEDIA

تشدید تنش‌ها در یمن و حملات حوثی‌ها به زیرساخت‌های حیاتی عربستان سعودی، آزمونی مهم برای رهبری این کشور ایجاد کرده است.

حملات به فرودگاه‌های ریاض و زیرساخت‌های انرژی، چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰ را تهدید می‌کند؛ برنامه شاخص محمد بن سلمان، ولیعهد عربستان، که هدف آن متنوع‌سازی اقتصاد و تبدیل عربستان سعودی به یکی از مراکز جهانی سرمایه‌گذاری، گردشگری و سرگرمی است.

این حملات همچنین می‌توانند به تلاش‌های عربستان برای ارائه تصویری از ثبات و امنیت آسیب بزنند.

در حالی که حملات ادامه دارد، چهره‌های مخالف حکومت عربستان می‌گویند محمد بن سلمان، حاکم عملی کشور، با «یکی از بزرگ‌ترین بحران‌های» دوران خود روبه‌رو شده است؛ آن هم در شرایطی که به گفته آن‌ها حمایت آمریکا کاهش یافته و کمک دیگر متحدان نیز محدود بوده است.

منبع تصویر، YOUTUBE/AL-ISLAH

احزاب سیاسی در عربستان سعودی ممنوع‌اند و حکومت مخالفت سیاسی را تحمل نمی‌کند.

به همین دلیل، اپوزیسیون سعودی از خارج کشور فعالیت می‌کند و شامل مخالفان اسلام‌گرای سنی، اصلاح‌طلبان لیبرال و طرفدار دموکراسی، فعالان حقوق شیعیان و منتقدان مستقل است.

یکی از سازمان‌یافته‌ترین اشکال اپوزیسیون «حزب مجمع ملی» است که کنشگرانی با پیشینه‌های مختلف را گرد هم آورده است.

رسانه‌های مخالف حکومت نیز وجود دارند، از جمله شبکه‌های تلویزیونی «الاصلاح» و «نبا» که ویدیوهایشان در یوتیوب صدها هزار بار دیده می‌شود.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

با شدت گرفتن حملات حوثی‌ها به عربستان در ماه اکتبر، مخالفان سعودی در تبعید، انتقاد از نحوه مدیریت جنگ از سوی حکومت را افزایش دادند و آن را شکستی توصیف کردند که کشور را بیش از پیش آسیب‌پذیر کرده است.

یحیی عسیری، فعال حقوق بشر و طرفدار دموکراسی، مخالفت قاطع خود را با حضور ریاض در جنگ اعلام کرد و در عین حال هرگونه «آسیب» به مردم، منابع یا زیرساخت‌های عربستان را رد کرد.

او در شبکه اجتماعی ایکس نوشت: «[حوثی‌ها] می‌دانند که ما مردمی تحت ستم و شکست‌ خورده‌ایم... کسانی که رنج می‌برند مردم محروم‌اند، در جنگی که خودشان انتخاب نکرده‌اند.»

او همچنین کشتار غیرنظامیان در همه طرف‌ها، از جمله در ریاض، شهر محاصره‌شده تعز در یمن و شهرهای صنعا و الحدیده تحت کنترل حوثی‌ها را محکوم کرد.

حزب او، «حزب مجمع ملی»، خواستار پایان جنگ شد و از رهبری عربستان خواست «از گرفتن تصمیم‌های بی‌پروا که همه ما را در معرض خطر قرار داده، دست بردارد».

علی الاحمد، مخالف شیعه، نیز از محمد بن سلمان خواست «این جنگ را تمام کند، به توافق برسد... و جان انسان‌ها را نجات دهد».

فواد ابراهیم، نویسنده و فعال شیعه، نیز در ایکس نوشت: «این بازی را متوقف کنید... دیگر کافی است... جز ورشکسته‌ها کسی دروغ‌هایتان را باور نمی‌کند.»

منتقدان همچنین به آنچه حمایت ناکافی آمریکا در جنگ می‌دانند و محدودیت‌های پیمان مکه با ترکیه و پاکستان اشاره کرده‌اند.

هرچند این پیمان به‌عنوان یک اتحاد دفاع متقابل مشابه ناتو معرفی شده بود، آنکارا و اسلام‌آباد تاکنون حمایت قابل توجهی از عربستان ارائه نکرده‌اند.

«صوت الناس»وب‌سایت ضد محمد بن سلمان، این پیمان را «نمایشی» توصیف کرده است.

تشدید درگیری همچنین انتقادها از اولویت‌های داخلی محمد بن سلمان را افزایش داده است.

مخالفان می‌گویند هزینه‌های هنگفت برای سرگرمی و پروژه‌های بزرگ توسعه‌ای به بهای تضعیف امنیت ملی تمام شده است.

درخواست‌ها برای پاسخگویی در فضای آنلاین گسترش یافته و برخی منتقدان می‌گویند محمد بن سلمان میلیاردها دلار در «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰» سرمایه‌گذاری کرده، اما نتوانسته امنیت کشور را حفظ کند.

سعید بن ناصر الغامدی، رئیس گروه حقوق بشری «سند» که بنا بر گزارش‌ها در بریتانیا درخواست پناهندگی کرده، در ۱۱ اکتبر در ایکس نوشت: «[محمد بن سلمان] جنگ [یمن] را آغاز کرد و کل کشور را وارد آن کرد... بعد با [حوثی‌ها در سال ۲۰۲۲] آتش‌بس امضا کرد و با آهنگ‌های سرگرمی، مهمانی‌های رقص و پروژه‌های خیالی آسوده نشست، در حالی که حوثی‌ها خود را برای نبردی طولانی آماده می‌کردند.»

منتقدان دیگر نیز به گسترش فعالیت‌های فرهنگی، رویدادهای ورزشی و کنسرت‌ها در عربستان اشاره کرده‌اند که پیش‌تر نیز با انتقاد روبه‌رو شده بودند.

برخی کاربران شبکه‌های اجتماعی در منطقه گفته‌اند این رویدادها با ارزش‌های اسلامی مغایرت دارند و پرسیده‌اند چرا حکومت «رویدادهای فرهنگی» را بر دفاع و امنیت منطقه‌ای مقدم دانسته است.

گروه مخالف «سعودی باس» گفت «شهروندان عربستان «زیر بار ترس زندگی می‌کنند»، در حالی که حکومت «درهای کشور را به روی رقص و آواز گشوده است».

صفحه «به سوی آزادی» در ایکس که ۱/۲ میلیون دنبال‌کننده دارد، ویدیویی از زنانی با پوشش باز در حال رقص در یک کنسرت منتشر کرد و نوشت: «اگر واقعا در مقابله با حوثی‌ها جدی هستید... این مهمانی‌های فاسد باید متوقف شوند.»

ترکی الشلهوب، روزنامه‌نگار مخالف، به ۱/۷ میلیون دنبال‌کننده خود در ایکس گفت «وعده‌های صنایع دفاعی» زمانی که عربستان با یک آزمون واقعی نظامی روبه‌رو شد «ناپدید شدند».

او پرسید: «پس میلیاردهایی که [به این صنعت] اختصاص داده شده بود کجا رفت؟!»

در میان آنچه مخالفان شکست‌های امنیتی می‌دانند، برخی از آن‌ها درخواست برای کنار رفتن حکومت را نیز شدت بخشیده‌اند.

برخی چهره‌های اپوزیسیون سعودی همچنین تاکید کرده‌اند که جنگ عربستان علیه حوثی‌ها به نفع اسرائیل تمام شده است.

دونالد ترامپ در ۱۶ اکتبر گفت ریاض از دریافت حمایت اسرائیل «بسیار خوشحال» است و عادی‌سازی روابط «بیش از هر زمان دیگری» دوباره مطرح شده است.

عبدالله العوده، عضو«حزب مجمع ملی» و پژوهشگر مقیم آمریکا، این کلیپ را در ایکس با هشتگ «عادی‌سازی خیانت است» به اشتراک گذاشت.

او همچنین هرگونه دخالت آمریکا در جنگ را رد کرد و گفت مردم و زیرساخت‌های عربستان «هزینه» این درگیری را می‌پردازند.

الغامدی نیز در ایکس گفت عربستان میلیاردها دلار را صرف رقص و ورزشگاه‌های فوتبال کرده و همین مسئله باعث شده با شروع حملات حوثی‌ها، برای کمک به اسرائیل روی بیاورد.

یحیی عسیری نیز در پستی در ۱۱ اکتبر گفت «کسانی که به جنگ دامن می‌زنند» فقط ثبات منطقه را تضعیف و «صهیونیست‌ها را تقویت» خواهند کرد.

وب‌سایت «سعودی لیکس» نیز از احتمال نزدیکی عربستان و اسرائیل سخن گفته و مدعی شده است اسرائیل در تازه‌ترین عملیات ضد حوثی‌ها در یمن مشارکت داشته است.

با نزدیک شدن به سال ۲۰۳۰، برنامه اقتصادی محمد بن سلمان برای کشور با موانع بزرگی روبه‌رو شده است.

منتقدان تاکید کرده‌اند که «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰»، طرحی بلندپروازانه برای متنوع کردن اقتصاد وابسته به نفت عربستان،  به ثبات و اعتماد سرمایه‌گذاران وابسته است. دو عاملی که جنگ منطقه‌ای آن‌ها را زیر سوال برده است.

مضاوی الرشید، استاد سعودی-بریتانیایی، در ایکس نوشت در حالی که تحلیلگران غربی «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰» را «ستایش» کرده‌اند، چشم‌انداز اقتصادی ریاض عملا به «موضوعی متعلق به گذشته» تبدیل شده است.

او همچنین گفت محمد بن سلمان «توانایی خود برای کنترل روایت موفقیت و رفاه» در رسانه‌های غربی را از دست داده است.

سعد الفقیه، رهبر «جنبش اصلاح اسلامی در عربستان» مستقر در لندن و مجری شبکه «الاصلاح»، گفت رسانه‌های غربی اکنون رهبری عربستان را «به تمسخر» می‌گیرند.

ترکی الشلهوب نیز در ایکس نوشت تمرکز بر «زرق‌وبرق و ظواهر» کار چندانی برای تامین امنیت شهروندان عربستان انجام نخواهد داد.

در جریان تازه‌ترین تشدید تنش‌ها، گزارش شده است که برخی حساب‌های مخالفان در داخل عربستان مسدود شده‌اند.

به گزارش گاردین، بیش از ۶۰ حساب مخالف سعودی در ایکس در ماه اوت مسدود شدند.

پیش‌تر، در ماه مه، کمیته حفاظت از روزنامه‌نگاران، از سرکوب پوشش رسانه‌ای جنگ با ایران در کشورهای خلیج فارس خبر داد و گفت در عربستان «پوشش مسائل سیاسی حساس به‌عنوان جرم علیه امنیت ملی تلقی می‌شود».

همان ماه، گروه حقوق بشری «سند» مستقر در بریتانیا گفت مقام‌های سعودی حساب‌های مخالفان را در تیک‌تاک، اسنپ‌چت و متا مسدود کرده‌اند و در تلاش‌اند این محدودیت‌ها را به ایکس نیز گسترش دهند.

در ماه اکتبر، هم‌زمان با حملات حوثی‌ها به زیرساخت‌های عربستان، غانم الدوسری، مخالف و کمدین مقیم بریتانیا، ریاض را متهم کرد که پس از انتشار مطلبی درباره قربانیان حمله حوثی‌ها به فرودگاه بین‌المللی ملک خالد، حساب او در ایکس را مسدود کرده است.

او با طعنه گفت: «با این حال، [عربستان سعودی] نتوانست موشک‌ها و پهپادهای حوثی‌ها را مسدود کند.»

news.originalContent:
Photo by Julia Beverly/Getty Images

A prominent ally of President Donald Trump says she won’t apologize for making money off her reputation.

Self-described journalist and activist Laura Loomer reportedly accepted thousands of dollars in undisclosed payments to write social media posts to her 1.9 million followers on X for clients who sought to reach the president, The Washington Post reported, citing former Trump campaign adviser Alex Bruesewitz and three anonymous sources. Loomer has been an influential voice among those in the president’s circle during his second term, having personally delivered information to him about National Security Council staffers she considered disloyal in April 2025 and urged him to fire them.

Loomer reportedly received $3,000 to $5,000, if not more, per commissioned social media post, according to the Post, citing two anonymous sources.

She and her media company, King Breaker Media, also appear to have received more than $60,000 across four payments since May 2025, according to bank records reviewed by the Post. These transactions may have served as payment for her X posts, two sources told the outlet, though the available financial records did not denote an explicit purpose. (RELATED: MAGA Influencers Are Wearing Out Their White House Welcome)

”I’m not some influencer that makes money from tweeting. My business is public affairs and opposition research,” Loomer said in an interview with the Post. She also denied the allegation she asks for $5,000 per tweet.

“Thank you to the Washington Post for promoting my public affairs company and my opposition research firm [Loomered Strategies] today in an effort to demonize me for… *checks notes* being effective,” Loomer wrote Saturday in an X post responding to the Post’s report. “Turns out it’s not illegal in America to make a living, and it’s not illegal to have a business doing public affairs and opposition research.”

Loomer is like a “nuclear bomb,” an anonymous source told the Post.

“A great Republican strategist, a great person, a killer when she’s angry at you,” Trump similarly said of Loomer at an Oct. 2 campaign rally.

Loomer is an advocate of the Iran War, which critics such as Tucker Carlson and former Republican Georgia Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene argue was a betrayal of the America First movement.

“WaPo claims in their smear article about me that I am a ‘nuclear bomb.’ They are right,” Loomer added. “You can hire me, or your opposition will.”

Thank you to the Washington Post for promoting my public affairs company and my opposition research firm today in an effort to demonize me for… *checks notes* being effective. Turns out it’s not illegal in America to make a living, and it’s not illegal to have a business doing public affairs and opposition research. Since when has it ever been a secret that I do oppo research and public affairs. People want to plant stories about me ahead of 2028 because many view me as a threat. They aren’t wrong, because when people look back at what I was capable of doing to previous campaigns, it’s work that even the most seasoned political consultants and opposition research firms are envious of. It’s work that has literally altered the course of history. It’s work that has been recognized by the most powerful people in the world. Some people want to plant stories about me because I suppose they worry that maybe they won’t be able to get me on their team ahead of 2028. 2028 is going to be a very busy year. news.originalContent:
Photo by Karen MINASYAN / AFP via Getty Images

An energy coalition is urging President Donald Trump to rein in Big Tech at a United Nations climate summit.

Six energy and policy groups warn that Amazon, Apple, and Google may hurt U.S. interests and break federal law by making “false and misleading” climate statements at the United Nations’ 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, according to a letter to the president shared exclusively with the Daily Caller News Foundation. All three companies profit from federal business despite working against the White House’s withdrawal from U.N. climate efforts, the groups argue. Because all three trade on public markets, the letter notes, they answer to federal oversight through the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Amazon, Apple, and Google each did not immediately respond to the DCNF’s requests for comment. Furthermore, the companies’ attendance at COP31 was unable to be confirmed at the time of writing.

The letter’s signatories are the American Energy Institute, the Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow (CFACT), the Energy & Environment Legal Institute, Heartland Impact, The Heartland Institute, and Truth in Energy and Climate.

“We applaud President Trump for pulling the US out of the UN climate hoax [sic]. But not all Americans have gotten the message,” Steve Milloy, a senior fellow at the Energy & Environment Legal Institute, said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation. “We are concerned that technology companies like Amazon, Apple and Google—companies that are government contractors with national security obligations—are nevertheless participating in COP31.”

“The President should bar federal contractors with national security obligations from participating in a process that only works to the benefit of Communist China,” he added. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: America’s Electric Grid Could Throw Wrench In Big Tech’s AI Dreams)

Milloy served on Trump’s Environmental Protection Agency transition team after the 2016 election, according to E&E News.

“Not only are these companies misleading the public and potentially violating the law by giving the public and investors the impression that they are doing something about supposed ‘climate change,’ but they are also undercutting U.S. foreign policy and national security by participating in COP31,” the letter states in part.

The letter goes on to call on the president to inform U.S. companies they are legally required to be honest and have a duty not to harm national security.

Cameron Sholty, the executive director of Heartland Impact, told the DCNF that the demand to power AI has pushed Big Tech toward natural gas and nuclear, warning that new climate pledges at the conference could harm those projects.

“Executives should also choose their proclamations carefully,” he said. “A COP31 podium provides no exemption from American law.”

The president’s withdrawal from the Paris Agreement would “cancel another 0.1°C of the progress” on projected warming this century, a 2025 U.N. emissions report states.

The U.N.’s 2026 report attributed “about half” of a roughly 0.2–0.3°C increase in its global warming forecasts to the U.S.’s “abandonment” of its climate pledge.

COP31, a conference which runs from Nov. 9-20, is the annual meeting for the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, an environmental treaty Trump moved to withdraw the U.S. from on Jan. 7. He similarly withdrew the U.S. from the U.N. Paris Agreement, which aims to limit compliant countries’ greenhouse gas emissions, for the second time Jan. 20, 2025.

Editor’s note: This report was updated with a statement from Cameron Sholty.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

A former MAHA adviser is asking Susie Wiles and two Trump-linked lobbying firms to preserve records tied to the allegations he aired on Joe Rogan’s podcast.

Calley Means named Wiles, Ballard Partners and Continental Strategy in a post on X. He asked for records of meetings, policy calls and the access lobbyists were given, according to the post.

Means sought records involving Bayer, Monsanto and the glyphosate executive order, sugar-industry fundraising tied to federal nutrition policy, and lobbying invoices, meeting calendars and visitor logs. The request covers encrypted and disappearing messages, he wrote. (RELATED: White House Staffers Undermined Pesticide Reform Over ‘National Security,’ Former MAHA Adviser Alleges)

Means tied the move to reports that Wiles and former White House Deputy Chief of Staff James Blair were weighing a lawsuit over the interview, according to his post. Blair disputed that account on X, saying he warned Means he would consider suing if defamed. “Calley, your poor me act is tiring and embarrassing for a grown man,” Blair wrote.

In light of suggestions that Susie Wiles and James Blair may pursue legal action over my Joe Rogan interview, I am publicly requesting that she, Ballard Partners, Continental Straregy, and other relevant parties immediately preserve all potentially relevant records and communications, including: ✅All communications between Susie Wiles, Ballard Partners, and their representatives concerning lobbying access, meetings, policy decisions, and corporate clients. ✅All communications involving Bayer, Monsanto, Ballard Partners, and White House officials concerning glyphosate, the national security executive order, and the administration’s position in Supreme Court litigation involving Bayer. ✅All communications concerning sugar-industry political contributions, fundraising commitments, and discussions about how those interests related to federal nutrition policy. ✅All communications involving Tony Fabrizio, food-industry representatives, and White House officials concerning MAHA initiatives, school nutrition standards, and the proposed federal definition of ultra-processed foods. ✅All drafts, internal correspondence, meeting notes, and communications involving Walker Barrett, Heidi Overton, and other relevant officials concerning the glyphosate executive order and Bayer litigation, including discussions about Secretary Kennedy’s involvement. ✅All relevant lobbying agreements, invoices, payment records, meeting calendars, visitor logs, and communications concerning corporate efforts to influence the policy decisions discussed in my interview - including from Continental Strategy. ✅All nonprivileged communications concerning my allegations, their factual accuracy, and any contemplated legal action arising from my interview. This preservation request includes emails, text messages, Signal, WhatsApp, encrypted or disappearing messages, attachments, drafts, and relevant electronically stored records. I welcome a full and transparent examination of the facts.

The fight grew out of Means’ appearance on the “Joe Rogan Experience” released Friday. He resigned Oct. 22. Means said he quit over what he called corruption inside the administration.

Wiles told him she needed sugar-industry money to win the midterms, Means said in the interview, The Hill reported. He also described being handed the glyphosate order for review. Walker Barrett, the assistant to the president for policy, called it final and told him to tell Health and Human Services Secretary (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy Jr. that “this is not up for discussion,” Means said.

President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14387 on Feb. 18, invoking the Defense Production Act to secure domestic supply of glyphosate-based herbicides and elemental phosphorus, according to the Federal Register. The Supreme Court ruled 7-2 on June 25 that federal pesticide law bars state failure-to-warn claims against Monsanto, a Bayer subsidiary.

Means alleged Heidi Overton, now Trump’s FDA pick, worked with the Justice Department on why the court should take Bayer’s case, The Hill reported.

Spokeswoman Allison Schuster previously told the Daily Caller News Foundation (DCNF) the administration already secured extensive victories for the MAHA agenda. A White House official called Wiles essential to that work. She hands the job to Stephen Miller on Friday.

“I welcome a full and transparent examination of the facts,” Means wrote.

دکتر کریستین بولیو، متخصص تغذیه، این را زنگ خطر می‌داند. او به شواهدی اشاره می‌کند که نشان می‌دهد، هرچه دو ساعت پیش از خواب بیشتر بخورید، «احتمال» افزایش وزن و چاقی «بیشتر» می‌شود.

خب، چرا هوس خوردن در شب این‌قدر رایج است و برای مهارش چه کاری از دستمان برمی‌آید؟

به‌رغم اینکه هنگام خواب مدتی طولانی‌ بی‌غذا می‌مانیم، طبق پژوهش‌ها، اشتهای ما به‌طور طبیعی عصرها به اوج می‌رسد تقریبا فارغ از اینکه در طول روز چقدر خورده‌ایم.

جیمز بتز، محقق دانشگاه باث، درباره نحوه پردازش غذا و انرژی در بدن می‌گوید، یکی از عوامل مهم این است که «هورمون گرسنگی» ما، یعنی گرلین، معمولا اواخر روز بالاتر است: «هرچند وعده‌های غذایی معمولا این هورمون را سرکوب می‌کنند، این اتفاق در واقع فقط بعد از اولین وعده روز می‌افتد، نه بعد از ناهار یا شام.»

اما اینکه چه می‌خورید هم مهم است. غذاهایی که پروتئین و فیبر و حجم زیادی دارند، معمولا مدت بیشتری ما را سیر نگه می‌دارند.

آقای بتز می‌گوید که اگر شامتان مغذی و پروپیمان نباشد، ممکن است انرژی‌تان یک‌باره افت کند و همین باعث می‌شود سراغ تنقلات بروید.

بعضی‌ها هم از ترس اینکه نیمه‌شب گرسنه بیدار شوند دیروقت چیزی می‌خورند؛ عادت هم نقش دارد.

سوزان هیگز، متخصص اشتها در دانشگاه بیرمنگام، می‌گوید: «اگر خوردن تنقلات اغلب در یک شرایط مشخص اتفاق بیفتد، محرک‌های محیط می‌توانند هوس خوردن را برانگیزند. مثلا اگر کسی معمولا موقع تماشای تلویزیون تنقلات بخورد، فقط روشن کردن تلویزیون ممکن است هوس خوردن را در او بیدار کند.»

فقط حس گرسنگی نیست که اواخر روز بیشتر می‌شود. پژوهش‌ها نشان می‌دهد که اشتهای ما برای غذاهای پرکالری هم قوی‌تر می‌شود؛ اشتهایی که سیستم پاداش مغز آن را پیش می‌برد، نه نیاز واقعی به انرژی.

دکتر بولیو که هم در دانشگاه لیدز و هم در دانشگاه مونکتون کانادا کار می‌کند، می‌گوید: «علاقه و میل ما به غذاهای پرچرب، در مقایسه با غذاهای کم‌چرب، اواخر روز بیشتر است. این میل لذت‌جویی می‌تواند بر نشانه‌های سیری غلبه کند و باعث شود با اینکه سیریم، دلمان تنقلات یا دسر بخواهد.»

حتی بعد از یک شام مفصل، غذاهای شیرین یا چرب یا شور همچنان می‌توانند مسیرهای پاداش مغز را فعال کنند و همین توضیح می‌دهد که چرا خیلی‌ها باز هم دستشان به سمت خوراکی دیگری می‌رود.

پس اگر ساعت ۹ شب خودتان را جلوی بیسکویت دیدید، شاید مشکل کمبود اراده نباشد، این قوانین زیست‌شناسی‌ است که مقابل‌تان ایستاده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

شواهد ضدونقیض است اما قطعا خوردن غذای سنگین در دیروقت بر گوارش و آمادگی بدن برای خواب اثر می‌گذارد.

تنقلات چطور؟ اینجا نتایج پژوهش‌ها چندان روشن نیست.

شواهدی وجود دارد که غذاهای سرشار از کربوهیدرات‌های تصفیه‌شده و قندهای افزودنی، از نان سفید و برنج سفید گرفته تا بیسکویت و کیک، ممکن است با خواب بد ارتباط داشته باشند.

به نظر پژوهشگران، دلیلش این است که چنین غذاهایی نوسان‌های بزرگ‌تری در قند خون ایجاد می‌کنند و ممکن است برخی از پیام‌های هورمونی را که در تنظیم خواب و اشتها نقش دارند، تغییر دهند.

ولی تشخیص علت و معلول دشوار است و ممکن است برعکس باشد، شاید کسانی که بدخوابی دارند بیشتر سراغ تنقلات شیرین بروند.

جاناتان جانستون، متخصص خواب و ساعت بدن در دانشگاه ساری، می‌گوید: «می‌دانیم کم‌خوابی نه فقط اشتها را زیاد می‌کند بلکه میل به غذاهای پرانرژی را هم افزایش می‌دهد.»

به اعتقاد جیمز بتز، به همین دلیل نمی‌شود با قطعیت گفت که خوردن تنقلات در دیروقت خواب را به هم می‌زند یا نه: «شواهد اصلا روشن نیست و شاید نشان دهد که واکنش آدم‌ها به غذاهای مختلف پیش از خواب با هم فرق دارد.»

اول، ببینید چه چیزی شما را به خوردن تنقلات وامی‌دارد:

سوزان هیگز می‌گوید: «خوردن درحالی‌که حواسمان پرت است، مثلا موقع تماشای تلویزیون، می‌تواند باعث بیشتر خوردن شود چون کمتر به مقدار توجه می‌کنند.»

اما به باور دکتر بولیو، لازم نیست تنقلات شبانه را کاملا ممنوع کرد:

«اشکالی ندارد گاهی خوراکی‌هایی را که هوسشان را کرده‌اید، به اندازه بخورید.»

به گفته او، ترفند مناسب این است که مبنا یک انتخاب سالم باشد: «اگر خوردنی‌های وسوسه‌انگیز همیشه در کابینت نباشند و  اگر هستند گزینه‌ای سالم باشند، احتمال اینکه گزینه سالم‌تر را انتخاب کنید، بیشتر می‌شود.»

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images)

American soldiers need generators to run their radios and sensors, but the noise and heat can help enemy drones find them.

As drones and electronic warfare gear move down to small field teams, the Army and the Pentagon’s Defense Innovation Unit are turning to companies that build hybrid battery systems so troops can shut generators off.

“There’s no way to turn that off, or you’re kind of faced with this really bad decision, which is, you know, turn off the generator, but then lose all of my communications, all of my sensors, right, or leave it on and be a target,” Chariot Defense CEO Adam Warmoth, whose company makes hybrid power systems, told the Daily Caller News Foundation.

Republican North Carolina Rep. Pat Harrigan, who served in Afghanistan as an Army officer and sits on the House Armed Services Committee, said a unit’s efforts to stay hidden are wasted once an enemy drone senses the warmth of its generator.

“You’ve just given away your position,” he said in a statement to the DCNF.

Harrigan added that he is “absolutely interested in funding hybrid generators and battery systems that can take some of that risk off our soldiers” in the next defense bill.

“I want to know how much quieter they are, how long they can operate without resupply, and whether they can handle the demands of a combat deployment,” he said.

Harrigan led Democratic nominee Ashley Bell by about 3,000 votes in the Nov. 3 race for the 10th Congressional District, according to unofficial returns from the North Carolina State Board of Elections. He is set to hang on to his seat despite the nationwide blue tsunami causing a cascade of Democratic flips in the state.

The military’s standard-issue power sources “generate noticeable acoustic and thermal signatures,” which can make it harder for units to operate quietly, the Defense Innovation Unit wrote in a request for portable battery systems that closed in March.

“Generators are loud. They create a lot of visual signature. They create a lot of thermal signature, and we have to get past that,” Army Chief Technology Officer Alex Miller said at a defense industry conference near Detroit in August, Breaking Defense reported. (RELATED: The War Against The Machines Has Arrived)

Cummins, which makes the service’s Advanced Medium Mobile Power Source generators, did not immediately respond to the DCNF’s request for comment.

Warmoth, whose company is based in San Bruno, California, said one big lesson from Ukraine “is just how much electronic capability is needed.”

Command posts, sensors and counter-drone systems used to run from relatively safe areas in the rear, according to Warmoth.

“That’s all now getting pushed down to these mobile distributed units,” he added.

Not long ago, a platoon or company had only a couple of radios to keep charged, Warmoth noted. Now units are leaving their trailer generators behind because towing slows them down.

“That heat and noise that’s making them a target” is the other reason, he said.

Air conditioners, lasers and radars create “really high demands that end up sizing your generator,” Warmoth said.

“You end up bringing, say, a 30 kilowatt generator, which is 2,300 pounds, even though your average demand for power is maybe only two kilowatts,” he said.

An Army paper published in August 2025 found the same thing. During a training exercise for a 101st Airborne Division brigade, its 15- and 30-kilowatt generators frequently ran at less than 10 percent of capacity, the paper said.

“The problem is they never do the maintenance in the field on the generators because they can’t turn them off,” Warmoth said. “Because if they turn them off, they lose all their systems.”

Dan Grazier, a senior fellow and director of the national security reform program at the Stimson Center, said he saw the challenge firsthand as a Marine Corps tank officer in Iraq in 2007. At least eight big diesel generators powered Camp Fallujah, and his platoon escorted fuel convoys that kept them running.

“They’re big, they’re loud, and they’re necessary because the U.S. military travels with a lot of things that require electricity,” Grazier told the DCNF.

Artificial intelligence systems need far more power than traditional ones, so “this problem is only going to get worse,” he said.

Defense Logistics Agency Energy, which supplies the military’s fuel, sold about 152.2 million gallons for the Army’s needs in the first nine months of 2026, the agency said in a statement to the DCNF. It referred questions about generator use to the service. (RELATED: Homegrown Power Could Keep The Army Running If War Cuts Off Foreign Fuel)

Chariot’s answer is a battery system that stores power from the vehicles and generators units already have, Warmoth said.

The smaller Amphora 24 hooks into the jump-start port on U.S. and NATO military vehicles and charges while they drive, he said. When a vehicle “gets where it’s going, it can turn its engine off and run all the system silently.”

“We can charge off a vehicle in say three hours,” he added.

For a command post running basic communications and sensing gear, “you’re looking at say six to eight hours” of silent operation, Warmoth said.

Chariot sees about 50 percent fuel savings, though it “depends a little bit on the load,” he said.

“You’re looking at double the runtime just based on that fuel savings,” Warmoth added.

Because the system handles power surges, units “can actually bring a smaller generator, or no generator at all, and just use the vehicle as the generator,” he noted, adding that this leaves room to carry more fuel.

“A unit operating with Chariot equipment could potentially operate for 300 hours,” Warmoth said, using the example of a unit that could run 100 hours on generators and batteries alone.

Separately, trucks rigged to send power from their engines have cut fuel use in Army testing. In an Army experiment called Project Convergence, the trucks used nearly 50 percent less fuel than the three to six “underused standalone generator sets” units had been running, according to an article the service published in fall 2024.

Chariot announced in August that the Defense Innovation Unit had awarded it a contract to supply Amphora systems to Army brigades over 12 months, with deployments planned to begin in fall 2026.

Most of the money goes to buying systems that active-duty units take into the field and on deployments, Warmoth said. The aim is to learn how much power units really use, since “that data realistically doesn’t exist.”

John Webber, New Use Energy’s vice president of sales, said in a statement to the DCNF that he visited two 101st Airborne Division teams using the company’s portable power units in the field at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, in October.
